analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as MALWARE with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams have positive SHAP contributions toward cryptojacking (+0.0087 to +0.0204). No n-gram pushes toward benign. The evidence does not list function names or per-function locations, so the analysis rests only on the mnemonic sequences and their frequencies. Several patterns are consistent with hashing or proof-of-work code. ROL ADD (+0.0124), MOV ROL (+0.0121), MOV SHRD (+0.0103) and SHRD BT (+0.0092) point to rotate and shift-based bit manipulation, which is typical of cryptographic mixing rounds. PXOR PXOR (+0.0108), PXOR MOVDQA (+0.0101), MOVDQA PAND (+0.0102, frequency 0.023), MOVDQA MOVAPS (+0.0141) and LEA MOVDQA (+0.0087) indicate heavy SSE vector use with XOR, AND masking and 128-bit data movement. That fits vectorized hash or memory-hard algorithm implementations. MOV MOVZX (+0.0165, frequency 0.058) and ADD MOVZX (+0.0097, frequency 0.016) indicate frequent byte-level loads and zero-extension, consistent with table lookups or byte-oriented transforms. Other n-grams are generic control-flow and stack patterns: POP SUB, MOV RET, CALL PUSH, PUSH RET, POP PUSH, POP CALL, POP XOR, LEA JC and DEC JZ. These are low in frequency and not specific to mining, but their rarity and high SHAP values suggest they mark unusual prologue/epilogue or dispatch structures that the model associates with the malware class. The case for cryptojacking comes from the combined crypto-style bitwise and SIMD patterns together with the model's maximal confidence. It is not proven by any single n-gram, and without function-level context the evidence is circumstantial.
